title: Proteus: Portable Runtime Optimization of GPU Kernel Execution with Just-in-Time Compilation
problem: AOT compilation optimizes GPU kernels with limited compile-time information, missing runtime specialization opportunities. Existing JIT approaches (e.g., CUDA Jitify) are language-specific and have high compilation overhead.
motivation: HPC applications benefit greatly from runtime specialization to input arguments and launch parameters, but AOT-compiled kernels miss these optimization opportunities.
method: Proteus compiles GPU kernels just-in-time (recompiling the code right before it runs rather than beforehand), using LLVM IR—an intermediate code format that works across programming languages. Users mark specific points in the code where it can be specialized for the actual input data and GPU launch settings. By using LLVM's portable infrastructure instead of language-specific tools, Proteus works across different GPU vendors without needing separate compilers.
key_novelty: Proteus is the first to use JIT compilation (compiling code right before it runs) on GPU kernels with language-agnostic code that works across all GPU vendors, delivering faster compilation than existing language-specific approaches.
contributions: Lightweight JIT compilation for GPU kernels via LLVM IR extraction
Portable across AMD and NVIDIA GPUs
Up to 2.8× speedup (AMD), 1.78× (NVIDIA); 1.23× faster than CUDA Jitify
limitations: Overhead of JIT compilation on slower GPUs not detailed; applicability to non-HPC workloads unclear.
